name: Kodak Professional BW400CN
notes: Chromogenic black-and-white film (C-41). The sheet plots THREE characteristic curves, B, G and R, in Status M (like a colour negative: their base levels differ, about 0.95 / 0.70 / 0.27 at the toe), not one neutral curve; they are traced as curves/b, curves/g, curves/r and there is no curves/v, so the sheet is not buildable as 'bw-negative' without choosing or deriving a neutral curve. The sheet itself says to treat the film like a colour negative (retouching, printing on colour negative paper: Portra Endura, Supra Endura, Ultra Endura or other colour negative papers), which is why print_on is left null here.
Characteristic curves: x axis is absolute log exposure in lux-seconds (daylight), Log H Ref -1.44 printed on the plot.

Spectral sensitivity: one curve, effective exposure 1/100 s, process C-41, Status M, density 0.2 above D-min; sensitivity/v. Log sensitivity = reciprocal of exposure (erg/cm2) as printed. The curve starts at about 390 nm and ends near 650 nm.

Spectral dye density (page 6): dyes/mid is the 'Midscale Density' curve (typical densities for a midscale neutral subject) and dyes/min the dashed 'Minimum Density' curve (D-min); diffuse spectral density, 400 to 700 nm. Both start at the left edge of the plot (400 nm) at a high value (about 2.15 and 1.5) and fall steeply in the first few nm.

Grain: Print Grain Index for 135 at 4x6 (4.4x) is printed only as 'less than 25' (25 is also the sheet's visual threshold of graininess), so pgi 25 is an upper bound; 135 at 8x10 (8.8x) = 40, 16x20 (17.8x) = 70; 6x6 cm (120/220): 4x6 and 8x10 'less than 25', 16x20 = 40.
Exposure latitude notes: the sheet gives no reciprocity compensation between 1/10,000 and 120 s and recommends nothing longer than 120 s; no push or pull speeds are given.
